column2: the plan never exempts the frontmatter `description:` trigger from compression, so the `use when ...` wording can be rewritten into a bare summary and trip `s017/desc-no-trigger`. if line 3 is shortened, the skill may stop advertising the `/design` trigger and agent-lint will reject the file before the plan can ship.

the compression brief does not mark `mandatory — read entire file` and `read … completely` clauses as non-compressible, even though those exact directive forms are what the closure scanner harvests. paraphrasing or splitting them removes direct markdown loads from `skill-closure report`; regen can drift closure membership while metric checks pass. this includes `read … design-background-wait.md completely` anchors (e.g. line 174), not only conditional step 4 mandatory lines; approach item 3’s invitation to collapse repeated read/apply prose increases that risk.

the `### updated: python/skill-closure-baseline.json` subsection and related plan baseline-update text end at "regenerate only through:" without naming the writer command. testing strategy also omits a `--write` step. an implementer following only the files/testing subsections can pass shrink checks yet skip baseline regeneration, hand-edit json, or guess a different writer, causing `test_committed_baseline_matches_fresh_scan` to fail in ci or a stale `python/skill-closure-baseline.json` to ship even though approach names `python3 python/cli.py lint skill-closure-growth --write` elsewhere.

plan.txt:82-87 `python/skill-closure-baseline.json` regeneration is still unspecified in the files block.. scenario: the plan tells the implementer to regenerate the baseline, but the `### updated: python/skill-closure-baseline.json` subsection is blank. a follower can guess the wrong writer or hand-edit json, which risks a stale baseline or a freshness-test failure.
